title: SBA run contract (business request)
description: The only input to the platform. Nine business fields: engine-neutral, provider-neutral in form, and business-only in content. Scope of this schema is GCP on GitHub Actions. Every technical value -- project, zone, machine type, image, network, labels -- is derived inside the platform from the reviewed catalogue. See AD-02 and docs/api/api-contract.md section 1. This schema is a control, not documentation: a field that is not here cannot reach a module, additionalProperties is false at every level so a nested object cannot smuggle one in, and a value that fails an enum is rejected at the trust boundary rather than passed to a module.

schema_version.description: Semantic version of this contract. Pinned by the caller, never derived from a request. A consumer must reject an unknown major with UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION; a minor bump is additive and unknown fields must be ignored rather than rejected. See AD-20 and docs/api/api-contract.md section 9.

request_id.description: The originating request number, e.g. a RITM number. Canonical, not user-supplied. This is the idempotency key and the run-state object prefix, so a re-submission of the same id resumes the same run instead of starting a second one, and a modified contract under the same id is REQUEST_MODIFIED rather than a silent overwrite. See AD-04 and docs/architecture/idempotency.md.

application.description: Business application code, chosen from the application register. Must be registered in configuration/applications/; an unregistered code is NO_APPROVED_CONFIGURATION and is never auto-created, because a catalogue that can self-populate is a catalogue nobody reviews. The code drives the project, the network tier, the cost centre and the owner group. See AD-19.

environment.description: Target environment. A control boundary, not only a label: it selects the policy floor, the GitHub Actions environment (and therefore its approval gate), the GCP project, and the workload identity federation subject. Derived from the register and cross-checked by the platform.

cloud.description: Cloud provider. Single-valued in this release: GCP only. The field is retained because it is part of the durable contract, and widening it is a minor bump under AD-20 -- an enum addition is additive and a consumer rejects an unknown member with UNSUPPORTED_ENUM_VALUE rather than passing it through. A closed set is the control that stops a buggy or compromised caller injecting a value that reaches a provider module. See docs/architecture/cloud/gcp.md.

region.description: Business region code, e.g. EU or US. Resolved to a GCP region such as europe-west1 through configuration/regions/. Must be inside the application's approved footprint. The concrete GCP region, and the zone within it, are deliberately NOT expressible here -- hence region_name and zone are forbidden properties. A zone that does not exist in the target region must fail at resolution, not at apply. See AD-19 and docs/architecture/cloud/gcp.md section 2.

server_role.description: What kind of server is wanted, chosen from the role register. Must be registered in configuration/server_roles/. The role determines the machine type floor, the disk shape, the baseline, and the required agents.

os.description: OS family, chosen from the OS register. A business choice with a technical consequence: it selects the pinned image entry, the CIS baseline, and the configuration and connection method. Closed enum -- an unvalidated string here would eventually reach a shell or a module argument.

count.description: How many servers. Bounded at 16 here as a transport ceiling, and bounded again per server_role and per environment by configuration/policies/; the tighter bound wins. An unbounded integer is a denial-of-service vector and count is the field a requester pushes hardest. Above the per-environment maximum this is QUOTA_EXCEEDED, never a silent clamp, because a clamp would report success for a build the requester did not get. On GCP this bound is additionally constrained by zone capacity at pre-flight, which is also not retryable. See docs/architecture/failure-and-retry.md section 2.

change_reference.description: The change record number backing an approved production change. Required when environment is PROD; that is the only conditional in this schema. The platform checks it is non-empty and may re-verify it, but approval authority itself is not duplicated inside the platform. See AD-17.

allOf.description: change_reference is mandatory in PROD. A schema-level control rather than a runtime check: a PROD request without a change record cannot be constructed at all, so it cannot be submitted, retried into existence, or produced by an automated caller that guessed. See AD-17.

change_reference.description: Change record number, e.g. CHG0012345. Required in PROD and permitted elsewhere, where it is retained for correlation with a change record that may be attached later.
